## Summary

I successfully implemented a bulk delete endpoint for items with the following features:

### Changes Made

**1. Added ItemBulkDelete model** (`backend/app/models.py`)
   - New Pydantic schema to accept a list of UUIDs for deletion

**2. Implemented POST /items/delete-many endpoint** (`backend/app/api/routes/items.py`)
   - Accepts a JSON payload with a list of item IDs
   - Validates that the list is not empty
   - Checks that all items exist before attempting deletion
   - Enforces authorization: users can only delete their own items; superusers can delete any items
   - Returns a success message after deletion or appropriate error responses

**3. Added 5 comprehensive tests** (`backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py`)
   - `test_delete_items_bulk`: Basic bulk delete with superuser
   - `test_delete_items_bulk_empty_list`: Validates error on empty ID list
   - `test_delete_items_bulk_not_found`: Validates error on non-existent item
   - `test_delete_items_bulk_normal_user_own_items`: Verifies normal users can delete their own items
   - `test_delete_items_bulk_normal_user_not_own_items`: Ensures users cannot delete others' items

**4. Enhanced test utilities** (`backend/tests/utils/`)
   - Updated `create_random_item` to accept optional `owner_id` parameter
   - Added `get_user_by_email` helper function to test utilities

### Key Features
- ✅ Authorization enforcement (users can only delete their own items)
- ✅ Superuser bypass (superusers can delete any items)
- ✅ Validation of all items before deletion
- ✅ All 16 item tests passing (11 existing + 5 new)
